transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-29
Time: 15:00 - 15:54 UTC
Duration: 54 min
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Rivera (Redwood SE), Alicia Moreno (Tellus Head of Search), Dev Bhattacharya (ML Eng), Samir Khan (CTO), Priya Das (PM)
Recording link: https://redwood.example/meetings/ff-20250529-8734 (placeholder)

Summary (auto):
Quick hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranking flow. Walked through Redwood Console, example API calls for embedding generation, vector search + rerank endpoint. Discussed latency targets, cost tradeoffs, and security (data residency/SOC2). Agreed next steps: share trial credentials, run small benchmark, and confirm pilot scope.

Topics covered:
- Current stack: Tellus currently uses Elastic + FAISS for vector store, precompute embeddings offline
- Redwood hosted embeddings endpoint and reranker pipeline
- Console walkthrough: model selection, scoring thresholds, telemetry
- Optimize recommendations: batching, KV cache, quant profiles
- Security: SOC 2, SAML SSO, KMS options, data retention & residency
- Pilot plan, success criteria (precision@5, end-to-end latency)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. Maya and Noah from infra/solutions.
[00:17] Alicia Moreno: Hey all, Alicia here. we run the Tellus search team. two goals today: understand hosted flow end to end, and see if latency works for our UI.
[00:29] Dev Bhattacharya: dev here, we'll be mainly concerned about throughput — we have ~200 requests/sec at peak and need to keep 99th under 600ms ideally.
[00:42] Maya Patel: great, that's helpful. i'll show our hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints, plus how the console surfaces latency/cost.
[00:50] Samir Khan: quick Q — data residency, can you keep data in eu-west? we have customers in EMEA.
[00:58] Noah Rivera: yes we have region routing, hosted api supports region pins — we'll share the doc URLs. there are sometimes slight perf diffs across regions.
[01:12] Jordan Lee: go ahead Maya.
[01:16] Speaker 1 (Maya Patel): I'm going to share my screen, bear with me while i open the Redwood console... ok see the model catalog here, for embeddings we recommend the med-quality open models for cost, or the high-perf for production. on the right you'll see token-cost estimates and a sample request.
[01:37] Priya Das: is the reranker a separate endpoint or is it integrated into the vector search?
[01:44] Maya Patel: good question. we typically do a two-stage flow: 1) dense vector retrieval for candidate recall using embeddings, 2) rerank endpoint that takes the query + top-K candidates and returns final ordering with scores. both are available via the hosted api.
[02:05] Dev Bhattacharya: are you returning embeddings as floats or quantized? we use 768-d floats now, cost is a concern.
[02:13] Maya Patel: embeddings are floats from the model, but we support model quantization on the inference side and recommend int8 in many cases — it depends on your quality tolerance. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles per workload.
[02:29] Alicia Moreno: can you demo a real call?
[02:33] Maya Patel: yeah i'll switch over to a notebook. here's an example POST to /v1/embeddings with our hosted key — note the small body and the sample response with vector dims. then we show a vector DB upsert example into their store (we demo with FAISS emu in the notebook).
[02:55] [02:55] Jordan Lee: (interrupting) for the cost numbers - remember that embedding generation per 1k docs at med quality is around X dollars — we'll send an updated cost table — but in short hosted is cheaper to get running quickly, dedicated reduces unit cost.
[03:10] Dev Bhattacharya: we have 10 million docs, we can't precompute everything every day, so we need incremental updates. how does your cache/batching help?
[03:20] Maya Patel: continuous batching on the runtime groups similar length requests to improve GPU utilization, and prefix/KV cache helps with chat style reuses. for embedding-only workloads, we also offer streaming and bulk endpoints.
[03:33] Alicia Moreno: what about reranker model latency? our UI block times out after 700ms.
[03:40] Noah Rivera: rerank latency is strongly dependent on K and model size — for a lightweight reranker we see P50 ~70ms P95 ~210ms in hosted tests for K=10 on latest gen GPUs; heavyweight cross-encoder models are higher. we can trade off by scoring top-100 with a mid-size model then final top-10 with the cross-encoder.
[04:05] Dev Bhattacharya: any public runs we can look at?
[04:09] Maya Patel: we've got perf profiles in the console and the model catalog — i'll attach the perf sheet after the call (link in notes).
[04:16] Priya Das: security again — how long do you retain inputs? our contract requires 90 day retention at most.
[04:25] Jordan Lee: by default hosted API does ephemeral storage for inference; we can configure retention, and there's an option to disable logging altogether for enterprise plans — we also integrate with customer KMS for key management.
[04:38] Alicia Moreno: we need SOC 2 Type II and SSO with SAML.
[04:44] Noah Rivera: we're SOC 2 attested, SAML/Okta is supported — we'll send the compliance pack.
[04:52] [05:00] (screen demo continues)
[05:12] Maya Patel: switching to rerank call— this is POST /v1/rerank with query + candidates array. sample payload returns score, rationale, and token-level alignment metadata. the console shows a confusion matrix if you run evals.
[05:37] Dev Bhattacharya: token-level alignment metadata? is that expensive to compute?
[05:44] Maya Patel: it adds overhead, but it's optional — you can toggle structured output for eval only.
[05:52] Alicia Moreno: what about integrating with our existing vector store? we don't want to migrate everything.
[06:00] Maya Patel: that's common; you can keep your FAISS/pinecone/weaviate store. the hosted API only needs the candidates passed into the rerank call — we don't require you to host vectors on Redwood.
[06:14] Dev Bhattacharya: hmm, and if we need to call rerank server-side for every query what's the cost model? per-call plus per-token?
[06:23] Jordan Lee: pricing for hosted rerank is a mix — per-request base + model compute tokens. i'll attach the pricing spreadsheet; for pilots we can offer credits.
[06:34] Priya Das: will the console let us track cost per route so product can allocate spend?
[06:40] Noah Rivera: yes route-level cost breakdowns, token-level drill-downs and alerts.
[06:47] [07:10] (Audience questions, short pause)
[07:20] Alicia Moreno: developer experience — our engineers must be able to iterate fast; do you have a local dev experience?
[07:28] Maya Patel: yes local SDK, and the quickstart notebook acts as a minimal reproducible example. we also have a dockerized inference shim for private deployments later.
[07:38] Dev Bhattacharya: what's the recommended K for candidate retrieval before rerank? we're currently doing K=100.
[07:45] Maya Patel: K=100 is reasonable for recall; many customers use 50-200 depending on freshness. we've seen diminishing returns after 200 for most corpora. Optimize can run evals and recommend K based on precision@k.
[08:05] Jordan Lee: i want to call out a few tradeoffs: higher K increases reranker cost and latency but can improve downstream precision. also quantizing embeddings reduces storage/cost but may slightly affect recall.
[08:18] Samir Khan: question on SLA — what's your uptime SLA for hosted?
[08:23] Noah Rivera: hosted has a 99.9% SLA for API up requests; dedicated has higher throughput guarantees. i'll send the SLA doc.
[08:33] (some crosstalk, connection hiccup at Alicia's side)
[09:05] Alicia Moreno: sorry briefly dropped — okay back.
[09:12] Maya Patel: demoing the Optimize tab now — it suggested a batching window of 20ms for their traffic profile, and recommended a small int8 quant profile for the medium-quality model. there are toggles for auto-batching and cache TTLs.
[09:33] Dev Bhattacharya: what's auto-batching behavior under burst? we can't have tails spike.
[09:41] Maya Patel: autoscaler + burst capacity can absorb short spikes; smart routing can divert to a lower-cost model for non-sensitive routes if you want to prioritize latency.
[09:55] Priya Das: any customers similar scale to us?
[10:00] Jordan Lee: a couple retail customers at similar QPS, and a few marketplaces. i'll share references after the call.
[10:08] Dev Bhattacharya: let's talk about pilot scope quickly — Alicia, Priya do you have constraints?
[10:15] Alicia Moreno: we want a quick proof: 10k doc slice, integrated in our staging UI, measure precision@5 and p95 latency for rerank end-to-end. two week trial would be ideal.
[10:28] Maya Patel: that sounds straightforward. we can provision a trial key and share a notebook showing the entire flow.
[10:34] Jordan Lee: action — Jordan shares trial and pricing. Maya runs the bench. Alicia provides sample data and criteria.
[10:42] Dev Bhattacharya: one more technical Q — do you support caching of rerank outputs? e.g., for repeated queries, we want to avoid reranking every time.
[10:50] Noah Rivera: yes there's a query result cache layer with TTLs, and you can use hashed candidate signatures to invalidate. it's configurable per route.
[11:03] Priya Das: ok good. we need a note on encryption in transit and at rest.
[11:08] Jordan Lee: TLS in transit, and at rest encryption via managed KMS or your own KMS — both options supported.
[11:18] Alicia Moreno: how do we estimate cost for 10 million corpus and 200 qps?
[11:24] Jordan Lee: we'll send a cost model worksheet — quick ballpark is that hosted will be higher per-unit than dedicated once you hit sustained volume — that's where reserved capacity benefits kick in.
[11:40] (demo wraps up, showing sample responses and logs)
[12:02] Maya Patel: last thing — evals in console can run A/B comparisons across model families and surface regression alerts if new model drops precision on your test set.
[12:15] Dev Bhattacharya: that could help us detect drift. do you store eval data?
[12:22] Maya Patel: we store eval meta; actual PII/documents are kept per your retention policy; eval traces are optional.
[12:34] Priya Das: any obstacles to getting started? legal? procurement?
[12:39] Jordan Lee: common blocker is security review and SOC2 docs — we'll send a compliance pack and our standard DPA. procurement usually needs a simple SOW for pilots.
[12:50] Alicia Moreno: timeline — can we start pilot the week of 6/9?
[12:54] Jordan Lee: yes, if we get the sample data this week we'll provision keys and schedule Maya's benchmark run.
[13:03] (wrap-up)
[13:12] Jordan Lee: to recap, i'll share trial creds, pricing sheet, perf profile links, and compliance docs. Maya will run a small latency test and report back. Alicia will share 10k sample and success criteria.
[13:28] Noah Rivera: attaching docs: perf-sheet (link), SOC2 pack (link), API quickstart (link).
[13:35] Alicia Moreno: thanks everyone. looking forward to the notebook.
[13:40] Dev Bhattacharya: thanks — we'll evaluate and circle back.
[13:45] (call ends shortly after)
